name: GrapeLeads
summary: Lead-finding for web developers and agencies: surfaces local businesses without websites from Google Maps, with contact details, on signup credits.
best_for: web developers, designers and agencies prospecting local businesses that do not have a website yet: surfaced from Google Maps with contact details
skip_if: you sell to companies that already have an online presence, or you want transparent pricing before creating an account
honest_knock: You are billed per result, not per usable lead: one credit opens the search and one more is charged for every business it returns, so a broad filter burns credits whether or not the results are worth calling. The packs are small enough that this is cheap to test ($28 for 50 credits) but it is the wrong shape if you want volume prospecting at a predictable monthly cost: there is no subscription at all. The site also still 404s its own /pricing link while the real list sits at /buy-credits/, which is an odd look for a tool sold to web professionals. And the niche (Google-Maps businesses without websites) is the real product: judge the data on one pack before you go further.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-27, read on their own buy-credits page; every amount unchanged since 12 August) Pay-as-you-go credit packs, bought once rather than subscribed to: Freelancer $28 for 50 credits ($0.56 each), Startup $55 for 100 credits ($0.54) and Agency $127 for 250 credits ($0.51). Bulk pricing is on request and signing up gives 20 free credits. Credits measure work, not leads: one credit starts a search and one more is charged for every filtered result, so a search that returns 20 matching businesses costs 21 credits. The vendor also states that unused credits carry a 50% bonus when its 2.0 app ships. Mind the URL — the price list lives at /buy-credits/ while the /pricing link 404s, which is how we had this down as unpriced until now. One rounding note: the page prints $0.54 per credit for the Startup pack, but $55 for 100 credits is $0.55 — their own figure is a cent optimistic.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested the free GrapeLeads preview, which gives 20 credits to an email address with no card. Of three searches one found 0 leads, one used a credit and never sent results, and one gave 11 leads after about 20 minutes. By our count 6 of those 11 were usable, about 2 credits per usable lead. Start: there is no app or account, only a search page with a map box, a business type and filters, an email pop-up and a results email. The free preview gave 20 credits to an email address; no card, password or phone number was asked. Our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab on 19 November 2026 from 12:02 to about 12:35 CET. The pop-up asks for the email address again for every search. Core action, three searches: Confirm Order says You have 20 credits remaining. Proceeding will use one credit for the search, and one credit for each result obtained. Search 1, Roofer in Dallas without websites: the email came after about 3 minutes with 0 Leads, 14 Raw Query Results, 1 Credits Used, so every roofer already had a website and the credit bought nothing. Search 2, Hair Salon in San Francisco without websites and with a phone number: no results email came within 25 minutes, not even in junk, yet the next confirm screen showed 18 credits. The search used 1 credit and returned nothing, with no error or status in the app. Search 3, Landscaping in Indianapolis without websites: the email came after about 20 minutes with 11 Leads, 121 Raw Query Results, 12 Credits Used, You have 6 credits remaining, and Errors: While processing the results, we had problems matching metadata for 19 establishments. In all 14 of 20 credits were used. The confirm screen never shows what the results will cost. Lead quality of the 11 landscaping leads, counted by hand (operational, phone, at least 1 rating, really a landscaper): 6 of 11 usable, 4 of 11 in the searched city itself; 2 sat about 55 and 70 miles away, one had no phone, one was not a business. A web check of 3 usable leads found no own website. At 12 credits for 6 usable leads that is 2 credits per usable lead, about $1.0 to $1.1 at pack prices. Limits: Business Type is a fixed list of 12 types, Categories are limited for this preview; the map box opens on a random city and moves only by dragging. Export is a CSV link in the email, valid 7 days, with company name, website, status, phone, address, rating and a Grape Lead Score. Plans: /pricing gives Page not found; Buy credits lists Freelancer $28 for 50 credits ($0.56 each), Startup $55 for 100 ($0.54) and Agency $127 for 250 ($0.51), all One-time, Secure checkout with Stripe. The results email says Each lead costs one credit, which is the equivalent of $0.30 per credit in bulk. Checkout: the card moment is Buy Now on the credits page; it was not clicked. Cancelling: there is no subscription and no account with a login, so there is nothing to cancel. Not tested: buying credits, the Stripe checkout, bulk pricing, asking for the lost credit back under the guarantee, and other cities. Clean up: the email address keeps 6 credits and an unconfirmed newsletter sign-up. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The confirm screen never says what the results will cost. A search can use a credit and send nothing, without an error. The map box opens on a random city. The pop-up asks for the email address on every search.
